reviewed_clauses.verbatim_extracted_text:
Initial MA
In accordance with relevant EU legislations, as transposed into Luxembourg legislation, no medicinal product may be placed on the market without prior authorisation. If a pharmaceutical company wishes to obtain an MA, it must file an application with the competent authority(ies). The application must include the results of analyses conducted on the medicinal product and research and development reports: industrial development (quality), pre-clinical trials, clinical trials, scientific literature, etc.
Once the application has been submitted to competent authority(ies) – in eCTD format –, it will then be evaluated, and an opinion issued on the balance benefits and risks. If the opinion is positive, the competent authority will deliver an MA.
An MA may be granted at European level or national level. Marketing authorisation applications may be filed using one of the following procedures:
The
Centralised Procedure (CP)
:
the MA is granted by the European Commission following a positive opinion from the
European Medicines Agency
(EMA)
. The MA is granted for all EU Member States (+ Norway, Iceland and Lichtenstein),
and published here
. This procedure is mandatory for innovative products, such as anti-cancer drugs.
The
Decentralised Procedure
(DCP): an initial MA is granted for the EU Member States chosen by the applicant.
The
Mutual Recognition Procedure
(MRP): if an initial MA has already been granted in an EU Member State, the applicant may decide to register the medicinal product in other EU Member States of their choice, based on the dossier that has already been assessed.
When an MA is granted through the
MRP and DCP
procedures
, the assessment is shared between the Member States.
The
National Procedure
: the MA is granted by a National Medicines Agency, and is only valid in that country. This procedure is only possible if an MA has not yet been granted in any other EU country.
